about: The melody's rules, the streaming that judges where a line splits into voices, and the figure space (public/shared/performers/melody-rules.js, streams.js, figure-space.js; docs/FIGURE_SPACE.md): one set of rules for every planner of a line, and every figure a point among dimensions, its named figures locations within them.

melody.about: The melody's rules, said once (public/shared/performers/melody-rules.js; docs/FIGURE_SPACE.md): what a line of pool steps may do, for every planner of one -- a motif's shape, a phrase's contour, a run, a figure, a cadence (line.js, figure-space.js). The owner, 5 November 2026: "where multiple scattered rules have been written that actually accomplish the same result, refactoring those rules into a smaller number will mean that fixing erroneous cases will lead to better generative behaviour more quickly." A leap's least and greatest size and a run's most moves are the line's (line.js LINE, a player's own: personality.js).

recoverMost.reason: a leap's answer: a step back the other way, of one or two of its voice's pitches (a second, or in a pool of close pitches a third) -- the recovery the lines' motifs, contours and runs had each asked (line.js recovered, shapeCells, simplifyMotif, contour, runContour)

alikeMost.reason: a note struck at most twice running, and so never three alike (the line's rule since its motifs were first made: line.js), unless a line asks for none struck again at once

streaming.about: Auditory streaming (public/shared/performers/streams.js; docs/FIGURE_SPACE.md): where a figure's notes hold together as one line and where they split into voices, a compound melody. The owner, 5 November 2026: "the 'musically correct' way to conceptualize two alternating notes far apart from each other (really, this intuition applies the more the further the notes are from each other and the faster they move/alternate) is as a compound melody"; "there is a threshold past which ornamentation transitions to compound melody". The boundaries it judges between are measured of listeners: registry/perception/streaming.json. A room's reverberation, which lengthens what sounds of each note, is not heard here (research/MODELING_GAPS.md).

threshold.unit: share from the fission boundary to the coherence boundary
threshold.reason: where a note is judged apart, a voice of its own, as a share from the fission boundary to the temporal coherence boundary (registry/perception/streaming.json): at the coherence boundary, as a listener in general tries to hear the tones as one line (van Noorden 1975, section 4.6), and between the boundaries hears them so but for attending to one string alone. There too Miller and Heise's trill threshold stands at its gap (perception trill-threshold). A legato whole tone so stays a trill up to about 13 notes a second, a semitone past 25

figure-space.about: The figure space (public/shared/performers/figure-space.js; docs/FIGURE_SPACE.md): every figure that divides a held note, a cadence's approach or a fioritura -- a run, an arc, an arpeggio, a trill, a turn, a mordent, a climb, a zigzag, a ribattuta, a compound melody, and every figure between or beyond them -- a point among dimensions, each a share 0 to 1, each named figure a location of ranges [low, high] within them (the methods figure-<name> below). A figure's path is made from its point, and its notes are the walk nearest that path that keeps the melody's rules (melody-rules.js), a trill only where its point asks for one. The owner, 5 November 2026: "(1) generalization of logic without losing cases ... (2) extensibility to arbitrary and invented ornaments beyond the specific figures listed".

third.reason: a third: two of its voice's pitches (a skip, the stride of an arpeggio and the width of a wide circling pair)

beam.reason: how many of its walk's settings are kept at each note, those with the same future kept once (as runContour's beam, line.js)

jitter.reason: a walk's ties broken at random by at most this, far less than a step from its path: the figure is its point's, the draw only choosing among walks as near

skew.reason: a skewed dimension's share drawn squared across its range (`skewed`): most figures circle little, turn as they circle rather than trill, strike few notes again and keep to one voice -- a trill, a turn, a ribattuta or a compound melody now and then, every figure still drawn (ours; the owner, 5 November 2026: figures "that simply alternate between two notes" were to stop)

skewed.reason: the dimensions whose draws are skewed toward their least (`skew`): circling, its pairs kept to one side (a trill), notes struck again, and voices

pair.reason: a circling pair and each step of an excursion: out and back, two moves

voiceNotes.reason: the fewest notes each voice of a compound figure has: two, so that it goes on as a line (one alone is a note heard apart, not a voice)

figure-arc.about: An arc: out from the held note the other way, then past the next note and back to it, by step (a fioritura, as Chopin's run past the note it lands on: fioritura.js).

lead.reason: its turn below and its arc above in any share

placement.reason: not read: it does not circle

figure-arpeggio.about: An arpeggio: its path by thirds.

lead.reason: its turn and arc in any share

placement.reason: not read: it does not circle

figure-trill.about: A trill: its spare notes alternating with a neighbour, toward the end (a cadential trill) or throughout.

trilling.reason: every pair to the side of the pair before

order.reason: from the upper note or the lower

figure-turn.about: A turn: its spare notes circling the held note on either side in turn, near its start.

figure-mordent.about: A mordent: a quick alternation with a neighbour at its start, the rest a walk.

trilling.reason: its pairs, where it has more than one, to one side: a short trill (a Pralltriller)

figure-climb.about: A climb: up two steps and back one as it goes, a pair at a time (a run turning back as it moves on).

progress.reason: each pair moving on a step

figure-zigzag.about: A zigzag: a wider climb, each pair a third wide -- up three steps and back two as it goes.

figure-ribattuta.about: A ribattuta: its notes struck again, each twice at most.

placement.reason: not read: it does not circle

figure-compound.about: A compound melody: the figure walking among voices far enough apart, at its rate, to be heard as voices (streams.js) -- a broken chord, a saxophone's chord played as a very fast arpeggio -- each voice moving evenly from the held note's chord to the next note's, the held note's voice the one that leaves them least to move.

voices.reason: as many voices as stream apart

idiom.about: An instrument's idiom told its player as relations, each a region of its items' joint space (public/shared/performers/idiom.js; research/IDIOM_AS_RELATIONS.md): a move's cost on its instrument by its direction, register and time, the notes it plays together, the hand's states; a line's search charged them, a player's daring carrying it toward the idiom's edge.

weight.unit: a move's cost a unit of -log of the share of its time it leaves (none for a move needing no time, 0.69 at half its time, without bound toward all of it), against the line's other costs (a pool step from where it is wanted 1, a rule broken 60), at a daring of 0 and of 1
weight.reason: ours: a cautious player's line keeping well within its instrument's idiom, a daring one's near its edge; beyond its edge a rule broken, whatever its daring

beyond.unit: a move's cost in a figure's walk where it needs more time than it has
beyond.reason: ours: as a rule the line breaks (line.js RULE), far dearer than any way from the figure's path, so that a figure makes a move its instrument cannot only where no walk keeps its rules without it

share.unit: share of the way toward the band's idioms, a round
share.reason: ours: how far a round of the piece's negotiation moves its weights toward what its instruments' idioms favour, so that the rounds settle (a contraction) and never reach the idioms alone: the seed's draw stays the prior (research/IDIOM_AS_RELATIONS.md, "Back through the player, over the piece")

themes.about: A line's themes over its piece's form (public/shared/performers/themes.js; bots/lib/modules/line-themes.js; line.js): which theme a phrase states and how it varies it, from its section's formal role in the conductor's form (plex_clodbot, mh_PlexBOT's archetypes: stochastic-config.js plex) and its player's lean toward restating (personality.js `themes`). The owner, 6 November 2026: "the soloist musebot's compositions tend not to be catchy and memorable because, even when the personality might want them, they lack most methods for recognizably repeating themes, I believe because the metrical structure keeps shifting throughout instead of taking shape according to a form." A theme keeps its rhythm and shape in any meter (line.js refitMotif), and what its notes divide into wherever it comes.

treatments.unit: how a section in each formal role treats a line's theme
treatments.reason: ours, after the sections of a classical form (W. E. Caplin 1998, Classical Form): a section that states its theme (the opening, and the calm after a climax) begins with it as it was first stated, from its first note; one that develops it (a departure, a development, a climax) sequences and inverts it; one that contrasts (a contrasting middle, and the frame's stable middle) brings a theme of its own, as unlike the first as its slate holds (line.js chooseMotif); one that returns brings back the first, from its first note. A role it does not name develops.

developments.unit: the variations a phrase that develops its theme draws among, each as likely
developments.reason: ours: the line's own (line.js LINE.variations): its idea sequenced, two steps higher, or inverted

developing.unit: share of its player's lean toward restating, in a section that develops its theme
developing.reason: ours: a developing section restates its theme a quarter as often as a stating one, so that the theme is heard to return where the form returns
